The person ran a Claude Code CLI command (`claude mcp add --transport http graphify https://api.graphify.com/mcp`) and appeared to be attempting to register a remote HTTP MCP server named "graphify" with Claude Code. Claude clarified that this command needs to be executed in a terminal rather than the chat interface, and that Graphify is not available as a connector in the chat app. Claude confirmed the command syntax appeared correct for registering a remote HTTP MCP server and offered troubleshooting guidance: using `--header` for authentication requirements and `--scope project` or `--scope user` for scoping. Claude also referenced `claude mcp list` for verifying successful connection and pointed to the official MCP documentation at docs.claude.com. An alternative path via Settings → Connectors was mentioned for using a custom connector within the chat interface.

That's a Claude Code CLI command, so it needs to run in your terminal rather than here — this chat can't execute it, and the connectors available in this interface are managed separately from Claude Code's MCP config. (Graphify also isn't in the connector directory for this app, so there's no one-click equivalent to offer.)

For what it's worth, the shape of the command looks right for registering a remote HTTP MCP server named `graphify` with Claude Code. If it errors, the usual suspects are that the server needs an auth header (Claude Code accepts `--header` for that) or that you want it scoped to the project rather than your user config (`--scope project` or `--scope user`). Once added, `claude mcp list` will show whether it connected. The reference for the exact flags is at https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp.

If you were instead hoping to use Graphify from this chat, the path is Settings → Connectors → add a custom connector with that URL, assuming the server supports it.
